questions.q:
Consider the following statements about a nuclear fission reactor:
1. Uranium-235 splits readily after absorbing a slow (thermal) neutron, releasing more neutrons that sustain the chain reaction.
2. The moderator speeds up neutrons so that they can split more nuclei.
3. Control rods made of boron or cadmium absorb neutrons and regulate the reaction.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Fission neutrons are fast, so a moderator (heavy water, light water or graphite) slows them down to thermal speeds where U-235 captures them efficiently. Control rods soak up surplus neutrons to hold the chain reaction steady.
questions.s: Spectrum Science & Tech; NCERT Class XII Physics
questions.h: Moderator = brake pedal for neutrons; control rod = off-switch.

questions.q: Which one of the following gives the correct sequence of the three stages of India's nuclear power programme envisioned by Homi Bhabha?
o: Fast breeder reactors, then PHWRs, then thorium reactors
PHWRs on natural uranium, then fast breeder reactors on plutonium, then reactors based on thorium and uranium-233
Thorium reactors, then PHWRs, then fast breeder reactors
Light water reactors on enriched uranium, then PHWRs, then fast breeder reactors
questions.e: India has modest uranium but vast thorium. Stage I PHWRs burn natural uranium and yield plutonium; Stage II fast breeders use that plutonium and breed more fuel; Stage III uses thorium converted into U-233.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Thorium cannot by itself be used to start and sustain a nuclear chain reaction.
Statement-II: Thorium-232 is a fertile material that must first absorb a neutron and change into fissile uranium-233.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Thorium-232 is fertile, not fissile. It absorbs a neutron, becomes Th-233 and decays through protactinium to U-233, which is fissile. This is why India's third stage depends on breeder reactors built in the earlier stages.

questions.q:
With reference to the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR) at Kalpakkam, consider the following statements:
1. It uses liquid sodium as coolant.
2. It uses heavy water as moderator.
3. It is being built by the public sector company BHAVINI.
4. It has a designed capacity of 500 MWe.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Fast reactors work with fast neutrons, so they have no moderator at all. They use a liquid-metal coolant, sodium, which does not slow neutrons. PFBR is a 500 MWe plant under Bharatiya Nabhikiya Vidyut Nigam Limited (BHAVINI).

questions.q:
Match the nuclear power sites in List-I with the features in List-II:
List-I: A. Kudankulam  B. Tarapur (Units 1 and 2)  C. Kakrapar (Unit 3)  D. Kalpakkam
List-II: 1. Prototype fast breeder reactor  2. Russian-designed VVER light-water reactors  3. Boiling water reactors  4. Indigenous 700 MWe PHWR
questions.e: Kudankulam (Tamil Nadu) has VVER-1000 units built with Russian help. Tarapur's first two units are India's oldest BWRs, and Kakrapar-3 in Gujarat was the first 700 MWe PHWR to start up. Kalpakkam is the fast reactor hub.

questions.q: Under the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT), a nuclear-weapon state is defined as a State that manufactured and exploded a nuclear device before which one of the following dates?
questions.e: This cut-off recognises only the USA, USSR, UK, France and China as nuclear-weapon states. India, which tested in 1974 and 1998, rejects the treaty as discriminatory and has never joined it. 1 July 1968 is when it opened for signature.
questions.s: Spectrum Science & Tech; UN treaty text

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Nuclear Suppliers Group (NSG) was formed in the mid-1970s in response to India's 1974 nuclear test.
Statement-II: India has been a full member of the NSG since it received a waiver in 2008.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The NSG was set up after Pokhran-I exposed the diversion risk of civil nuclear material. The 2008 waiver only lets India trade in civil nuclear material and technology; India's membership has not been granted.

questions.q:
Arrange the following events in India's nuclear history in chronological order:
1. Pokhran-I test
2. Pokhran-II tests
3. NSG waiver for civil nuclear trade with India
4. Operationalisation of India's nuclear doctrine
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: The order is 1974, 1998, January 2003 (doctrine reviewed and made public by the Cabinet Committee on Security) and September 2008 (NSG waiver).

questions.q: Under the Civil Liability for Nuclear Damage Act, 2010, legal liability for nuclear damage is primarily channelled to which one of the following?
o: The operator of the nuclear installation
The supplier of the reactor equipment
questions.e: The Act makes the operator, such as NPCIL, strictly liable without proof of fault. Suppliers face only limited right of recourse, which has been the main sticking point in foreign reactor deals.
questions.s: Spectrum Science & Tech; PRS Legislative Research

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about the Apsara reactor?
o: India's first commercial power reactor at Tarapur
A fast reactor at Kalpakkam using plutonium fuel
Asia's first research reactor, a swimming-pool type at Trombay that became critical in 1956
A reactor at Kudankulam built with Russian help
questions.e: Apsara at BARC, Trombay, was commissioned in August 1956. India's first commercial plant was Tarapur (1969), and the fast reactor at Kalpakkam is the FBTR.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Nuclear fusion combines light nuclei into a heavier nucleus and releases energy.
2. The ITER project is being built at Rokkasho in Japan.
3. India is a member of the ITER project.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Fusion releases energy because the product nucleus has higher binding energy per nucleon. ITER, a tokamak, is under construction at Cadarache in southern France, and India is one of its seven members.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct regarding nuclear fusion as compared to fission?
o: It involves splitting of heavy nuclei such as uranium
It occurs readily at room temperature
It produces large quantities of long-lived high-level waste like fission
It requires extremely high temperatures to overcome the electrostatic repulsion between the nuclei
questions.e: Nuclei are positively charged and repel; only at temperatures of millions of degrees, as in the Sun's core or a tokamak plasma, do they approach closely enough to fuse. Fusion does not create fission-type long-lived waste.

questions.q: Which of the following accidents have been rated at the highest level, level 7, on the International Nuclear and Radiological Event Scale (INES)?
o: Fukushima Daiichi and Three Mile Island
questions.e: Chernobyl (1986) and Fukushima Daiichi (2011) are the only two level 7 events. Three Mile Island (1979) was level 5.

questions.q: A radioactive isotope has a half-life of 10 years. What fraction of the original sample will remain after 30 years?
questions.e: Thirty years is three half-lives, so the fraction left is (1/2) x (1/2) x (1/2) = 1/8. Radioactive decay is exponential, not linear, so it does not drop by a third each period.
questions.h: Halve it each time: 1, 1/2, 1/4, 1/8 after three half-lives.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of radioisotope and use is NOT correctly matched?
o: Carbon-14 : dating of rocks that are billions of years old
questions.e: Carbon-14 has a half-life of about 5,730 years and is useful only for organic remains up to about 50,000 years old. Rocks are dated with long-lived isotopes such as uranium.
questions.h: C-14 is for once-living remains; for rocks use uranium.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:
1. Natural uranium contains only about 0.7 percent of the fissile isotope uranium-235.
2. PHWRs can use natural uranium because heavy water absorbs very few neutrons.
3. Light water reactors can run on natural uranium without enrichment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Light water absorbs neutrons readily, so it needs fuel enriched to a few percent U-235. Heavy water is a far better moderator in this respect, so natural uranium works in PHWRs.

questions.q: Which one of the following minerals is the main source of thorium in India?
questions.e: Monazite occurs in the beach sands of Kerala, Tamil Nadu and Odisha and also supplies rare earths. Pitchblende (uraninite) is a uranium ore.

questions.q:
With reference to India's nuclear doctrine, consider the following statements:
1. India follows a policy of no first use and does not use nuclear weapons against non-nuclear-weapon states.
2. Retaliation to a nuclear attack on India is to be massive, to cause unacceptable damage.
3. The Executive Council of the Nuclear Command Authority is chaired by the Chief of Defence Staff.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Political Council, chaired by the Prime Minister, alone authorises use; the Executive Council is headed by the National Security Adviser. The 2003 doctrine also keeps a credible minimum deterrent.
questions.s: PIB / Cabinet Committee on Security, Jan 2003

questions.q: Which one of the following is an advantage of Small Modular Reactors (SMRs)?
o: Each unit must exceed 1,000 MWe to be viable
They must be built entirely on site and cannot be factory made
They can be factory-built in modules, suiting smaller grids and captive industrial sites
They operate only on nuclear fusion
questions.e: SMRs (generally up to about 300 MWe) are meant to be built in factories and shipped, cutting construction time and risk. The Union Budget 2025-26 announced a Nuclear Energy Mission to develop indigenous SMRs.

questions.q: Tritium, needed as fuel for future deuterium-tritium fusion reactors such as ITER, is expected to be bred from which element?
questions.e: Tritium is scarce in nature. Neutrons from the fusion reaction strike lithium in the reactor's blanket and produce tritium, so the plant can make its own fuel.

questions.q: Which one of the following units is used to measure the biological effect of ionising radiation (equivalent dose)?
questions.e: The sievert accounts for the type of radiation and tissue sensitivity. The becquerel and curie measure activity (disintegrations per second), while the gray measures the energy absorbed per kilogram.

questions.q: Which one of the following Indian research reactors uses uranium-233 as fuel?
questions.e: KAMINI at Kalpakkam is a small research reactor fuelled by U-233, which is bred from thorium, and fits with the thorium route of the three-stage plan. Dhruva and Cirus used natural uranium.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant?
o: It has fast breeder reactors using plutonium
It uses natural uranium with heavy water as moderator
It has VVER-1000 pressurised light-water reactors built with Russian assistance
It uses thorium as its primary fuel
questions.e: Kudankulam in Tamil Nadu has Russian-designed VVER-1000 units, which are enriched-uranium light-water reactors under IAEA safeguards. It is not a PHWR or a breeder.

questions.q: What is a 'dirty bomb'?
o: A bomb that uses a fusion reaction triggered by plutonium
A fission weapon that uses highly enriched uranium
A neutron weapon that spares buildings
A conventional explosive combined with radioactive material to spread contamination
questions.e: A dirty bomb, formally a radiological dispersal device, has no chain reaction. It spreads radioactive material, causing contamination and fear rather than nuclear-scale destruction.

questions.q:
Statement-I: The Sun's energy comes from nuclear fusion of hydrogen into helium in its core.
Statement-II: At the extremely high temperature and pressure of the solar core, hydrogen nuclei can overcome their mutual electrostatic repulsion and fuse.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: The solar core is around 15 million kelvin, and hydrogen nuclei move fast enough, helped by quantum tunnelling, to approach closely and fuse. This is the proton-proton chain, releasing the energy radiated by the Sun.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the International Solar Alliance (ISA):
1. It was launched by India and France at the Paris climate conference (COP21) in 2015.
2. Its headquarters is in Gurugram, India.
3. Only countries lying between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn can be its members.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The ISA began with sunshine-rich countries between the tropics, but its framework was amended in 2020 to admit all UN member states. So statement 3 is no longer true.
questions.h: ISA: born in Paris 2015, home in Gurugram.

questions.q: A solar cell generates electricity from sunlight on the basis of which one of the following?
o: Photoelectric effect, where electrons are ejected from a metal surface
Thermionic emission from a heated cathode
Photovoltaic effect at a semiconductor p-n junction
questions.e: Light creates electron-hole pairs in the semiconductor, and the built-in field at the p-n junction separates them and drives a current in the circuit. In the photoelectric effect, electrons escape from the material altogether.
questions.s: NCERT Class XII Physics; Ramesh Singh

questions.q: Which one of the following statements about solar energy technologies is NOT correct?
o: Photovoltaic cells produce electricity from sunlight using a semiconductor p-n junction
Concentrated solar power uses mirrors to focus sunlight and heat a fluid that drives a turbine
Perovskite solar cells are being developed as a low-cost option with potentially high efficiency
Concentrated solar power converts sunlight directly into electricity with no heat stage
questions.e: CSP is a solar thermal technology: mirrors concentrate sunlight, the heat makes steam and a turbine generates power. Direct conversion of light into electricity is photovoltaics.

questions.q:
With reference to India's climate commitments announced at COP26 (Glasgow), consider the following statements:
1. India will achieve 500 GW of non-fossil fuel electricity capacity by 2030.
2. India will meet 50 percent of its installed electric power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030.
3. India has updated its target to reduce the emissions intensity of its GDP by 45 percent by 2030 from the 2005 level.
4. India will reach net-zero emissions by 2060.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The Panchamrit pledges set 2070, not 2060, as the net-zero year. The other three targets are correct, and the 45 percent emissions intensity target was formalised in India's updated NDC (2022).

questions.q: The PM Surya Ghar: Muft Bijli Yojana, launched in 2024, targets rooftop solar installation in how many households?
questions.e: The scheme aims at rooftop solar for one crore households, providing up to 300 units of free electricity a month, with central financial assistance. It is run by the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.

questions.q:
Which of the following are components of the PM-KUSUM scheme?
1. Standalone solar agricultural pumps
2. Solarisation of grid-connected agricultural pumps
3. Solar street lighting in municipalities
4. Small solar power plants of up to 2 MW on farmland
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
questions.e: PM-KUSUM (2019) helps farmers with decentralised solar plants up to 2 MW, standalone solar pumps and solarisation of existing grid-connected pumps. Municipal street lighting is not a component.

questions.q: The power available in the wind is proportional to the cube of the wind speed. If the wind speed at a site doubles, the power available in the wind increases by a factor of:
questions.e: Since power varies as v cubed, doubling v gives 2 x 2 x 2 = 8 times the power. This is why turbines are sited in high-wind areas and mounted on tall towers.
questions.h: Wind power goes with the cube: double the speed, eight times the power.

questions.q: The Union Government has approved viability gap funding for the first offshore wind projects off the coasts of which pair of States?
questions.e: The 2024 approval supported 1 GW of offshore wind projects, 500 MW each off Gujarat and Tamil Nadu, where wind resource assessments were strongest. India's offshore wind policy dates from 2015.

questions.q:
With reference to the National Green Hydrogen Mission, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in January 2023.
2. It targets 50 million tonnes of green hydrogen production a year by 2030.
3. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas is the nodal ministry.
4. It aims to make India a net importer of green hydrogen.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: The mission aims at about 5 million tonnes a year by 2030, not 50, and seeks to make India a global hub and exporter. The nodal ministry is the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.

questions.q:
Match the types of hydrogen in List-I with their production methods in List-II:
List-I: A. Green hydrogen  B. Grey hydrogen  C. Blue hydrogen  D. Brown hydrogen
List-II: 1. Steam methane reforming with carbon capture  2. Steam methane reforming without carbon capture  3. Electrolysis of water using renewable electricity  4. Coal gasification
questions.e: Green hydrogen uses renewable power to split water; grey and blue both come from natural gas, but only blue captures the CO2. Brown (or black) hydrogen comes from coal and has the highest emissions.
questions.s: National Green Hydrogen Mission; Ramesh Singh
questions.h: Green = water, Grey = gas, Blue = gas + capture, Brown = coal.

questions.q:
Statement-I: Hydrogen fuel cell vehicles emit only water at the tailpipe.
Statement-II: A fuel cell generates electricity by burning hydrogen in an internal combustion engine.
Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: A fuel cell combines hydrogen and oxygen electrochemically to give electricity, water and heat, with no combustion. Statement-I is therefore right but the stated mechanism in Statement-II is wrong.

questions.q: Which one of the following is correct about hydrogen as a fuel?
o: It has less energy per unit mass than petrol and more per unit volume
It has the highest energy per unit mass among common fuels but low energy per unit volume as a gas
It is available in large natural reserves that can be tapped directly
Burning it releases carbon dioxide and water
questions.e: Hydrogen carries about three times the energy per kilogram of petrol, but as a gas it takes a lot of volume, so storage needs compression, liquefaction or carriers. It is mostly bound in water and hydrocarbons and releases only water on use.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about lithium-ion batteries:
1. During discharge, lithium ions move from the anode to the cathode through the electrolyte.
2. Graphite is commonly used as the anode material.
3. Lithium iron phosphate batteries need a cobalt-rich cathode.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: On charging, the ions are pushed into the graphite anode, and on discharge they flow back to the cathode, driving electrons through the external circuit. LFP cathodes contain iron and phosphate, not cobalt.

questions.q: In February 2023, the Geological Survey of India established an inferred lithium resource of about 5.9 million tonnes in which one of the following places?
questions.e: The Salal-Haimana area of Reasi district was the first lithium resource of this scale in India. Mandya in Karnataka has a much smaller resource.

questions.q: In which type of rechargeable battery is the energy stored in liquid electrolytes held in external tanks, so that its power and energy capacity can be scaled independently?
questions.e: In a flow battery the electrolyte is pumped through a cell stack; larger tanks give more energy, and a bigger stack gives more power. This makes them attractive for long-duration grid storage.

questions.q: Why are pumped storage hydropower plants useful for power grids with a large share of renewable energy?
o: They store surplus electricity by pumping water to an upper reservoir and release it through turbines at peak demand
They generate more electricity than they consume
They produce electricity from tidal movements
They convert municipal waste into biogas
questions.e: Solar and wind output varies, so surplus power in the afternoon can lift water uphill and be recovered in the evening. They are net consumers of energy because of conversion losses, so they serve as storage, not as sources.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about biofuels:
1. First-generation biofuels are made from non-food lignocellulosic residues.
2. Second-generation biofuels use biomass such as crop residues and agricultural waste.
3. Third-generation biofuels are derived from algae.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: First-generation biofuels come from food crops such as sugarcane, maize and oilseeds. Second-generation ones use residues like straw and bagasse, and third-generation ones use algae.
questions.s: Ramesh Singh; National Policy on Biofuels 2018

questions.q: The SATAT initiative launched in 2018 is aimed at promoting which one of the following?
o: Compressed biogas as an automotive fuel
questions.e: SATAT (Sustainable Alternative Towards Affordable Transportation) invites entrepreneurs to set up compressed biogas plants and sell the gas through fuel retail outlets. Waste, such as agricultural residue and cattle dung, is the feedstock.

questions.q: Which one of the following was launched at the G20 Leaders' Summit in New Delhi in September 2023?
o: One Sun One World One Grid
questions.e: The Global Biofuels Alliance, with India, the USA and Brazil among its first members, was announced at the summit. CDRI came in 2019, the Big Cat Alliance in 2023 at Mysuru and OSOWOG at COP26 in 2021.

questions.q: India advanced its target of 20 percent ethanol blending in petrol from 2030 to which ethanol supply year?
questions.e: The Roadmap for Ethanol Blending in India 2020-25 brought forward E20 to 2025-26. The National Policy on Biofuels 2018 originally set 2030.

questions.q: Which one of the following pairs of place and renewable energy source is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gulf of Khambhat : Tidal energy potential
questions.e: Muppandal in Tamil Nadu is one of India's best known wind farm clusters. Puga and Manikaran are hot spring sites tapped for geothermal heat, and the Gulf of Khambhat has strong tidal range.

questions.q: Which one of the following solar parks is correctly matched with the State in which it is located?
questions.e: Pavagada is in Tumakuru district of Karnataka. Bhadla is in Rajasthan, Kamuthi in Tamil Nadu and Rewa in Madhya Pradesh.

questions.q: An electric heater of power 2 kW is used for 3 hours. Given that 1 kWh = 3.6 MJ, how much energy does it consume in megajoules?
questions.e: Energy = 2 kW x 3 h = 6 kWh, and 6 x 3.6 = 21.6 MJ. The value 6 is the figure in kWh, so it is not megajoules.
questions.s: NCERT Class X and XII Physics

questions.q: Which one of the following battery chemistries contains no cobalt or nickel and is valued for thermal stability and long cycle life?
questions.e: LFP uses iron and phosphate, which are cheap and abundant, and its structure is stable even when heated. It has lower energy density, hence common use in buses and stationary storage.

questions.q:
With reference to energy efficiency in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Bureau of Energy Efficiency was set up under the Energy Conservation Act, 2001.
2. The Bureau runs the Standards and Labelling programme (star ratings) for appliances.
3. The Perform, Achieve and Trade (PAT) scheme trades carbon credits among industries.
4. The Bureau functions under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: BEE (2002) works under the Ministry of Power. The PAT scheme trades Energy Saving Certificates earned by industries that beat their efficiency targets; carbon credit trading is a separate scheme.
questions.s: Ministry of Power; BEE; Ramesh Singh
